cases.sentence: Может быть, ___ Дулова тоже прославленная арфистка.
cases.translation: Perhaps Vera Dulova is a famous harpist too.
cases.explain: Вера Дулова is the subject of the sentence (she «is» a harpist), and subjects stand in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Я ему сначала кинул ___, прямо с порога.
cases.translation: First I threw the balalaika to him, right from the doorway.
cases.explain: The thing thrown is the direct object of the transitive verb «кинул», so it takes the accusative: балалайку.

cases.sentence: Выпить целый флакон ___, а потом поставить флакон на место.
cases.translation: To drink a whole bottle of ink and then put the bottle back in its place.
cases.explain: After a container word («флакон») the substance measured goes into the genitive; чернила is plural-only, so its genitive is чернил.

cases.sentence: У Ивана ___ все это немножко не так.
cases.translation: In Ivan Turgenev it is all a little different.
cases.explain: The preposition «у» (at someone's place, in someone's work) always governs the genitive: у Тургенева.

cases.sentence: Пошел я к ___ Эрдели, хотел объяснить, в чем дело.
cases.translation: I went to see Olga Erdeli, I wanted to explain what the matter was.
cases.explain: «К» meaning 'to (a person)' takes the dative, so Ольга becomes Ольге.

cases.sentence: Они там на ___ сидят и играют.
cases.translation: There they sit at their harps and play.
cases.explain: «На» answering «где?» (position, not direction) requires the prepositional; the plural prepositional of арфа is арфах.

cases.sentence: Чтоб я ее удавил ___ от арфы.
cases.translation: So that I would strangle her with a string from a harp.
cases.explain: The means or instrument of an action stands in the instrumental with no preposition: удавить струною.

cases.sentence: Я припомнил свою похвальбу в день знакомства с моей ___.
cases.translation: I recalled my boasting on the day I met my Queen.
cases.explain: «С» in the sense of 'together with' governs the instrumental: знакомство с Царицей.

reading.question: Who tells the first story in the compartment?
reading.explain: The chapter opens by saying that the Decembrist was the first to begin telling a story.

reading.ru: На Ольге Эрдели, прославленной советской арфистке.
reading.question: Who was the Decembrist's friend obsessed with?
options: Olga Erdeli, a famous Soviet harpist
A drunk woman with a balalaika
reading.correct: Olga Erdeli, a famous Soviet harpist
reading.explain: The friend went out of his mind over the harpist Olga Erdeli, whom he had only ever heard on the radio.

reading.ru: Может быть, Вера Дулова тоже прославленная арфистка.
reading.question: What does the Decembrist concede about Vera Dulova?
options: That she may well be a famous harpist too
That she plays much worse than Erdeli
That nobody has ever heard of her
That she does not play the harp at all
reading.correct: That she may well be a famous harpist too
reading.explain: He allows that Vera Dulova is perhaps just as famous, but insists the friend was fixated specifically on Erdeli.

reading.question: How did the obsession change the friend's daily life?
options: He lay in bed and gave up work, study, smoking and drinking
He started working two jobs to buy a harp
He travelled around Moscow looking for Erdeli
He learned to play the harp himself
reading.correct: He lay in bed and gave up work, study, smoking and drinking
reading.explain: He simply lay there: not working, not studying, not smoking, not drinking, not even leaning out of the window.

reading.question: How did his friends try to talk him into accepting a substitute?
options: By insisting that Vera Dulova plays beautifully
By promising to take him to a concert
By buying him a radio of his own
By telling him Erdeli had died
reading.correct: By insisting that Vera Dulova plays beautifully
reading.explain: They urged him to take Vera Dulova instead of Erdeli, praising her playing.

reading.question: What did the sick man threaten to do if they brought him Vera Dulova?
options: Strangle her with a harp string
Throw her out of the window
reading.correct: Strangle her with a harp string
reading.explain: He said they could drag her over only if they wanted him to strangle her with a string from a harp.

reading.ru: Малый совсем вымирает, надо его спасать.
reading.question: How did the Decembrist judge his friend's condition?
options: That the lad was dying out and had to be saved
That the lad was only pretending
That the lad would recover by himself
That the lad had already recovered
reading.correct: That the lad was dying out and had to be saved
reading.explain: He decided the young man was fading away and that something had to be done to rescue him.

reading.ru: Пошел я к Ольге Эрдели, хотел объяснить, в чем дело, да так и не решился.
reading.question: What happened when the Decembrist went to Olga Erdeli?
options: He wanted to explain the situation but never dared to
She agreed at once to visit the sick man
She refused him rudely at the door
He could not find her address
reading.correct: He wanted to explain the situation but never dared to
reading.explain: He got as far as going to her, but could not bring himself to explain; he thought of Vera Dulova too and gave that up as well.

reading.question: What was happening at the moment the idea struck him?
options: A very drunk woman had stopped him and begged for a rouble
He was listening to the harp on the radio
He was standing outside Erdeli's door
He was sitting at his friend's bedside
reading.correct: A very drunk woman had stopped him and begged for a rouble
reading.explain: The plan came to him while walking through evening Moscow, when a thoroughly drunk woman asked him for a rouble.

reading.ru: Я ему сначала кинул балалайку, прямо с порога.
reading.question: What did the Decembrist throw in first when he arrived with the woman?
reading.explain: He had made the woman bring a balalaika for greater persuasiveness and threw it in from the doorway before pushing her at his friend.

reading.question: What became of the friend after the visit?
options: He turned back into an ordinary human being
He grew even more obsessed than before
He took up the balalaika professionally
reading.correct: He turned back into an ordinary human being
reading.explain: Next morning he opened the window, had a quiet smoke, then went back to working, studying and drinking.

reading.question: What did the listeners demand instead of the harpist story?
options: A story about love, in the manner of Turgenev
A song accompanied on the balalaika
reading.correct: A story about love, in the manner of Turgenev
reading.explain: They interrupted, asking where the love and where the Turgenev were, and demanded a first-love story with Zinochka and the veil.

reading.ru: Ну, да ладно, у нас и без камина есть чем согреться.
reading.question: How does Venichka answer the fact that they have no Turgenevian fireplace?
options: They have something else to warm themselves with
They should light a fire in the carriage
They should go home and read Turgenev
reading.correct: They have something else to warm themselves with
reading.explain: He jokes that without a fireplace, and without jabots, they have drink to warm them — they are already speechless drunk.

reading.question: How does the Decembrist answer Venichka's question about the party office and the bottle of ink?
options: He admits he would not be able to do it
He says he has already done it once
He says he would do it for any woman
He refuses to answer at all
reading.correct: He admits he would not be able to do it
reading.explain: Asked whether he could drink a whole bottle of ink for the woman he loved, he says 'My God! No, I could not.'

reading.ru: Так неожиданно, что все снова заерзали и запотирали руки.
reading.question: How did the company react when Grandpa Mitrich suddenly spoke up?
options: They fidgeted and rubbed their hands in anticipation
They told him to be quiet
They pretended not to hear him
reading.correct: They fidgeted and rubbed their hands in anticipation
reading.explain: Mitrich's offer to tell a story came so unexpectedly that everyone started fidgeting and rubbing their hands again.

reading.question: How does Mitrich answer the charge that he has never read Turgenev?
options: He says his little grandson has read everything instead
He claims he has read all of Turgenev twice
He says books are of no use to anyone
He says he will read it on the way to Petushki
reading.correct: He says his little grandson has read everything instead
reading.explain: He does not deny it — he points to his grandson as the reader in the family, and the others promise the grandson a turn later.

highlight.question: Which sentence lists all the ordinary things the young man had stopped doing?
sentences: Помешался и лежит.
Не работает, не учится, не курит, не пьет, с постели не встает, девушек не любит и в окошко не высовывается…
Подай ему Ольгу Эрдели, и весь тут сказ.
Наслажусь, мол, арфисткой Ольгой Эрдели и только тогда – воскресюсь: встану с постели, буду работать и учиться, буду пить и курить и высунусь в окошко.
Мы ему говорим: – Ну зачем тебе именно Эрдели?
highlight.explain: The second sentence is the string of negated verbs describing everything he no longer does.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells what happened when the Decembrist actually went to Olga Erdeli?
sentences: Ну что делать?
Малый совсем вымирает, надо его спасать.
Пошел я к Ольге Эрдели, хотел объяснить, в чем дело, да так и не решился.
Хотел даже и к Вере Дуловой – да нет, думаю, удавит он ее, как незабудку.
И иду я по Москве вечером, и грустно мне: они там на арфах сидят и играют, толстеют и пухнут на арфах, а от малого остались руины и пепел.
highlight.explain: The third sentence says he went to her, meant to explain, and never brought himself to do it.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what he threw in first, straight from the doorway?
sentences: И вот – я поволок ее к моему приятелю.
Вошли: он все лежит и тоскует.
Я ему сначала кинул балалайку, прямо с порога.
А потом – швырнул ему в лицо эту Ольгу, я этой Ольгой в него запустил!..
«Вот она – Эрдели! Не веришь – спроси!»
highlight.explain: The balalaika came first, and only after it the woman he was passing off as Erdeli.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what the Decembrist saw the very next morning?
sentences: И наутро смотрю: отворилось окошко, он в него высунулся и потихоньку закурил.
Потом – потихоньку заработал, заучился, запил…
И стал человек как человек.
Вот видите!..
highlight.explain: The first sentence gives the morning scene: the window opening, the man leaning out and quietly lighting a cigarette.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes how such scenes look in Turgenev, with the fireplace and the top hats?
sentences: – Конечно, – прибавил я, – у Ивана Тургенева все это немножко не так, у него все собираются к камину, в цилиндрах, и держат жабо на отлете…
Ну, да ладно, у нас и без камина есть чем согреться.
А жабо – что нам жабо!
Мы уже и без жабо – лыка не вяжем…
highlight.explain: Only the first sentence describes Turgenev's world; the rest are about the travellers' own situation.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes the other passengers' reaction to Mitrich speaking up?
sentences: – А я бы смог! – проговорил вдруг дедушка Митрич.
Так неожиданно, что все снова заерзали и запотирали руки.
– А я бы смог чего-нибудь рассказать…
highlight.explain: The middle sentence reports the fidgeting and hand-rubbing his sudden offer produced.
